## QMD BODY — docs/guide/desktop-helper.qmd

---
title: "Desktop helper"
---

The session reviewer runs headless, and its wins are easy to miss: a PR opens while you are
deep in another session, merges while you are away, or the reviewer starts failing silently in
the background. Captain Hook.app closes that visibility gap. It is a small resident macOS app
that turns review lifecycle events into native notifications and puts the open reviewer PRs in
a Notification Center widget. It is an optional companion to the
[session reviewer](session-reviewer.qmd), not a requirement for it.

## What it is

Captain Hook.app is a Dock-less background agent (`LSUIElement`): no Dock icon, no menu bar
item, no windows. It is written in Swift on [DaemonKit](https://github.com/yasyf/daemonkit)
and does three things:

- serves the `~/.capt-hook/helper.sock` control socket and posts each accepted `notify`
  request as a native banner;
- ships a WidgetKit extension that renders the reviewer's open PRs from
  `~/.capt-hook/status.json`;
- keeps itself resident by reconciling a login-item registration (`SMAppService`) on every
  launch, so it survives reboots without you thinking about it.

Everything it knows arrives over the socket or the snapshot file. The app holds no state of
its own and never talks to the network.

## Install

The helper ships as a Homebrew cask — Developer ID signed, notarized, and stapled, so
Gatekeeper validates it offline and the first launch is silent. One command taps, installs,
and launches it:

```bash
uvx capt-hook helper install
```

Then two one-time grants in System Settings:

1. **Notifications** — allow Captain Hook under System Settings > Notifications.
2. **Widget** — add the review widget via Edit Widgets in Notification Center.

macOS may also surface the login item under System Settings > General > Login Items; the app
registers it itself on first launch, so approving the prompt is all there is to do.

Upgrades are hands-off: `brew upgrade --cask capt-hook-helper` replaces the bundle and
restarts the resident process, so the running helper is always the installed version.
Uninstalling through Homebrew unregisters the login item first, so quitting the app cannot
race an instant relaunch.

To build from source instead, run `helper/scripts/build-local.sh` from a captain-hook clone.
It generates the Xcode project, builds Release, verifies the App Group entitlement survived
signing, and swaps the result into `/Applications`. It signs with your Developer ID identity
(`CODESIGN_IDENTITY` / `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM`), never ad-hoc — identity churn resets the
notification-permission grant, so an ad-hoc build re-prompts on every rebuild.

## Notifications

Three kinds of banner, all fired by the reviewer as its state changes:

| Kind | Fires when | Click opens |
|---|---|---|
| `pr_open` | A candidate's pull request opens | The PR |
| `pr_merged` | A reviewer PR merges (the candidate is accepted) | The PR |
| `review_failure` | Three consecutive review runs fail | Nothing (no URL) |

The whole banner is the click target — there are no action buttons. A click opens the
notification's http(s) URL, so a `pr_open` banner lands you on the PR ready to review.
Banners thread by repo in Notification Center.

The `review_failure` banner fires once per failing streak, not once per failure: after the
third consecutive failed run it announces, then stays silent until a clean run resets the
streak. A reviewer that breaks and stays broken costs you one banner, not thirty.

Delivery never blocks review. The reviewer tries the socket; if the helper is not running it
launches the app in the background (`open -g -a "Captain Hook"`) and polls for a few seconds;
if the helper is not installed or stays unreachable, the notification is logged and dropped.
No exception ever reaches the hook path, and there is no `osascript` fallback — the lanes are
the socket and a logged drop.

## Widgets

The widget renders `~/.capt-hook/status.json` in three sizes:

| Size | Shows | Click |
|---|---|---|
| Small | The open-PR count and a health dot | The whole tile deep-links to the newest PR |
| Medium | A header row plus up to three PRs | Each row deep-links to its PR |
| Large | The same list, up to eight rows | Each row deep-links to its PR |

Each PR row shows the PR title, the rule it enforces, and how long it has been open. The
health dot is green while review runs succeed and flips when the reviewer is failing. A stale
snapshot dims the whole widget instead of showing fresh-looking numbers, and a machine
that never enabled review gets a "review not enabled" tile pointing at
`capt-hook review enable`.

## CLI

`uvx capt-hook helper` is the user-facing surface:

```bash
uvx capt-hook helper install   # tap, install/upgrade the cask, launch in the background
uvx capt-hook helper status    # ping the running helper, print its version
uvx capt-hook helper notify    # fire a test banner (launches the helper if needed)
```

`notify` takes `--kind` (`pr_open`/`pr_merged`/`review_failure`), `--title`, `--subtitle`,
`--body`, `--url`, and `--repo`, and prints which lane delivered:

```bash
uvx capt-hook helper notify --title "Hook PR opened" --url https://example.com/pr/1
```

```
lane=socket ok=True error=None
```

`lane=dropped` means the helper was unreachable and could not be launched — usually "not
installed yet".

## Protocol and trust

The helper serves `~/.capt-hook/helper.sock`: newline-delimited JSON, one request per
connection, LF-terminated, protocol version `v: 1`. Two ops exist — `ping` returns the
helper's version, `notify` posts a banner. Requests and replies are capped at 64 KiB per
line; an oversized notify request is dropped client-side before it touches the wire.

```json
{"v":1,"op":"notify","kind":"pr_open","title":"Hook PR opened","url":"https://example.com/pr/1"}
{"v":1,"ok":true}
```

The protocol is frozen: both sides are pinned byte-for-byte by shared golden fixtures under
`tests/fixtures/`, so the Python client and the Swift server cannot drift apart silently.

Trust is same-UID. The helper checks every connecting peer's credentials and only accepts a
process running as the same user — another user on the machine cannot post banners through
your helper. Clients are launch-on-demand: they connect first, and only when the socket is
unreachable do they start the app with `open -g -a`, so an idle machine runs the helper
exactly when something wants to notify.

## Snapshots

`~/.capt-hook/status.json` is the widget's entire world view: a `schema_version` 1 document
carrying per-repo candidate counts, the open PRs newest-first, and the reviewer's health. It
is written by exactly one codepath, atomically — rendered to a tempfile in the same directory,
then renamed into place — so the helper's directory watch sees one complete swap, never a
half-written file.

You rarely write it by hand. The reviewer writes it after every run, success and failure
alike, so a session end refreshes the widget for free. The helper also keeps it current on
its own, re-running the snapshot every ten minutes and shortly after each notification. The
manual command exists for scripting and debugging:

```bash
uvx capt-hook review snapshot            # project the review store into status.json
uvx capt-hook review snapshot --refresh  # sync each watched repo's open PRs first
```

`--refresh` folds in each repo's PR state through a TTL-cached GitHub read, so a PR you merged
in the browser shows up without waiting for a session to end. The command guards on an
existing review database — on a machine that never enabled review it prints
`no review database yet` and writes nothing.

PR titles come from the candidate: the reviewer's brain passes `--pr-title` when it records
the PR-opening move (`review update <id> pr_open --pr-url <url> --pr-title "<title>"`), and
the title persists across every later status move. Move a candidate by hand without it and
the banner and widget row fall back to a generic description — pass it.

The [desktop helper](desktop-helper.qmd) puts this queue on your desktop: a native macOS

a Notification Center widget listing the open PRs. It is optional — the reviewer runs fine
